 Order
The petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3, who are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Section 3(1)(s) and Sections 448, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC, are before this Court.
2. The respondent No.2 lodged the FIR alleging that, the complainant was working as Computer Operator in Ekadantha Couriers.

The petitioners - accused Nos.1 and 2 are the employees of Amazon Transportation Service Private Limited (for short `ATSPL') and petitioner - accused No.3 is the Authorized Representative of ATSPL, and when the complainant was operating the computer, at that time, the accused herein abused him in filthy language with reference to his caste on his mobile phone.
The registration of FIR is impugned in this petition.

sentences.text: 2 3. Sri Ashok Haranahalli, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner would submit that, the alleged incident has taken place on 28.12.2022, and the FIR was lodged on 13.1.2023 without offering any plausible explanation.
He further submits that, abusing of the complainant on phone does not come under the purview of public view so as to constitute the commission of offence under the provisions of the Atrocities Act.
He further submits that, the impugned FIR was lodged by the complainant as a counter blast to circumvent the FIR registered against Ekadantha Couriers, with whom the misappropriation of Rs.57 lakh.
Hence, the continuation of investigation will be an abuse of process of law.

4. The learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State submits that, the allegation made in the FIR discloses the commission of offences alleged against the petitioner, and the veracity of the allegation against the petitioner requires to be investigated, and at this stage, the registration of FIR does not warrant any interference.
5. Considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
6. The allegation is that the petitioners - accused herein, who are the employees of ATSPL, abused the complainant on mobile phone with reference to his caste.
Admittedly, abusing of complainant is not within the public view so as to constitute the commission of offences punishable under the provisions of the Atrocities Act.
The alleged incident has taken place on 28.12.2022 and the FIR was lodged on 13.1.2023 without offering any plausible explanation.

The petitioners - accused herein, who are the employees of ATSPL, had lodged the FIR in Crime No.20/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 406,
407, 420 read with Section 34 of IPC against the Ekadantha Couriers for having misappropriated a sum of Rs.57 lakh.
The complainant is the employee of Ekadantha Couriers.
Hence, it is inferred that the FIR was lodged by the complainant as a counter blast to circumvent the FIR registered against the Ekadantha Couriers.
8. In view of the preceding analysis, I am of the considered view that, the FIR was lodged with malice and without any probable cause.
Hence, the continuation of investigation will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned FIR in Crime No.16/2023 registered by the Chickamagalur Town Police Station, insofar as it relates to the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3 is hereby quashed.
